Palomino Blackwing Natural Pencil Review — The Pen Addict

# Palomino Blackwing Natural Pencil Review 

 

 

The Palomino Blackwing 602 has been my pencil of choice for years. I use pencils that are firmer, darker, lighter, or better looking on a regular basis, but I always go back to the 602. There is something about the feel and style of the pencil that draws me in. Blackwing’s Firm core has been perfect for me.

Based on my pencil core likes - firm, dark, good point retention - you think I would have latched on more permanently to Blackwing’s Extra Firm core when they first introduced it a few years ago in the Blackwing Volume 24 edition. I loved it, of course, yet for some reason, I kept reaching for the 602.

 

 

I think the reason was psychological. What if I use up all of these pencils and there are no more? So I wouldn’t use them. This errant line of thinking has been something I’ve been trying to erase from my stationery mindset over the years. Use the things I like whenever, wherever, and however I want, no exceptions.

 

 

In the case of the new Palomino Blackwing Natural, it took a stock offering of their fantastic Extra Firm core to save me from me. This core may be better for me than the Firm core in the 602, and I’ve been too stubborn to find out.

The Blackwing Natural was announced at the National Stationery Show back in February, and since their initial retail release in March, have been exceedingly hard to come by. They’ve appeared and vanished at all of my favorite retailers faster than I could buy them. It took a post-Atlanta Pen Show trip to Archer Paper for me to accidentally stumble on a box to purchase. Yes, a box of a dozen. Single pencils begone!

 

 

I took the Natural out for a spin last week to use with my CW&T Studio Sketchbook at my son’s baseball practice. This notebook is an excellent choice for pencils with its textured paper, and I have been using it for brainstorming product ideas and general doodles.

As I began writing, I just kept saying to myself “Huh.” As in, “Huh, this is better than expected, “ and “Huh, I’ve been missing out.” Don’t let the Extra Firm designation trick you into thinking the Natural is something along the lines of a 4H grade pencil. As someone who enjoys those H-grade nails, this is nothing like that at all. Palomino’s Blackwing designation of Extra Firm is in relation to the other cores in the lineup, which range from Soft to Balanced to Firm, to now Extra Firm.

 

 

Comparing one pencil core to another can be difficult when they are somewhat close. Slight differences in hand pressure can change everything, so view my tests and commentary with that in mind. That said, the Natural is as dark, or darker, than the 602. That is what’s confusing me. Can this really be firmer and darker than the 602 at the same time? And keep the same, or better, smoothness? Maybe so.

(Note: I ordered and tagged the Pearl and MMX incorrectly on the page. The Pearl is the Balanced core and the MMX is the Soft core, and they perform exactly that way.)

 

 

This brings me back around to the 24 edition. Did I miss this the first time around - over three years ago - because of some weird limited edition angst? And, miss future opportunities with the release of the 530, 54, and others, for the same reason? I only have my mindset to blame.

 

 

Visually, the Natural is everything that Blackwing fans have been clamoring for from the beginning. It was inevitable that Palomino would release a raw barrel in the lineup. It was also inevitable that once they released the Extra Firm core in the Volumes lineup that it would come to the stock lineup eventually. The combination of those two things is why they have been running behind in production and are hard to find right after release.

I still think the 602 is better looking, but I do love natural barrel pencils. I upgraded this one with an orange eraser, as I also do for my 602 pencils. All that’s left to wonder is if the Natural will take the top usage spot over from its stablemate in the long term. It may already have.

 

 

Posted on April 15, 2019 by Brad Dowdy and filed under Palomino, Blackwing, Pencil Reviews.

Compatible Products (1)

Blackwing pencils are ideal for illustrators and writers who prefer a soft, dark line. These Natural pencils are crafted from incense cedar wood with a clear matte finish, letting you appreciate the natural color and pattern of the wood. They feature gold imprinted writing on the barrels. The unique rectangular gray eraser can be extended as it wears down from use, and also pops out completely from the pencil body for replacement. The eraser is latex free, and replacement erasers are available in a variety of colors.

Blackwing pencils differ in the softness of the graphite core, which can be felt while writing and drawing. These pencils feature an extra-firm core that holds a sharp point without sacrificing dark lines. 

These pencils were previously known as Palomino Blackwing Pencils.

## Customer Reviews

- Thought I'd add my two...

February 13, 2020

Thought I'd add my two cents to the conversation. I have mixed thoughts on this pencil. The finish is nice for a natural-wood pencil. Nice and smooth without obscuring the wood tones. However, I do miss the small amount of weight and substance which seems to be added by the painted finish. Feels a bit "too light" to me, and unbalanced with the chunky ferule/eraser combo on the other end. As for the writing experience, it's decently dark for such a hard core. However, it feels incredibly scratchy and not at all like the experience of the 602. Between the finish and writing experience, one wonders how it's even in the same lineup as the rest of the smooth, dark Blackwings.

13 people found this helpful

Scotty A See all my reviews
- Needs quality control....

September 5, 2019 Verified Purchase

Needs quality control. The pencils are wonderful, but such an expensive box of pencils I expect all of them to be in good quality. One was split through, a few others had wood knotches in them. Felt a bit like I got a box of discards. 

12 people found this helpful

Nichole B See all my reviews
- These pencils are smoothest...

July 11, 2019 Verified Purchase

These pencils are smoothest pencils I have ever owned. The weight of this pencil feels very nice due to the added weight to the end of the pencil because of the metal eraser clip and the LONG eraser. The pencil sharpens very nice and has never broken during sharpening. The wood even feels smooth while sharping. Another positive thing about this pencil is that natural wood "look" of this pencil is made very nice and does not look like I shaved the yellow paint off a Ticonderoga pencil. The pencil holds its just as much as a normal HB pencil but writes very smooth and even darker. This pencil even under the lightest of pressure, writes darker than any HB pencil I have ever used. Compared to the most famous Ticonderoga pencil, the Ticonderoga pencil feels as if you are scratching your nail on a chalkboard when compared to the rich and smooth feeling of the Palomino Blackwing pencil. Not to even mention how aesthetically pleasing this pencil looks when compared to the yellow and green colors of the Ticonderoga pencil. I usually share my stationary products with fellow school mates, but the second I used this pencil, I knew that I wanted to keep every single piece of graphite of this pencil to myself. If this pencil was marked at twice the price, I will not hesitate to buy this pack of pencil again. All in all a 100/5.

9 people found this helpful

YellowPickles21 See all my reviews
- Sharpens to a VERY sharp,...

December 2, 2019 Verified Purchase

Sharpens to a VERY sharp, fine, long lasting point. Not gritty or fragile. This is my “go to” for ridiculously fine detail work. (I prefer the standard Blackwing for marathon writing and the Pearl for most everything though it is softer). Overall if you like pencils/graphite a lot, it is true that Palomino Blackwings are noticeably smoother and are a different experience than a plain old yellow #2. (In fairness I haven’t tried Tombow or Uni pencils as of this writing)

5 people found this helpful

MrTomRN See all my reviews
- Blackwing erasers continue...

April 2, 2021 Verified Purchase

Blackwing erasers continue to suck, but the graphite makes up for it. I fell in love with Blackwing's extra-firm graphite when they originally created with for Vol. 24 and am thrilled that they decided to make it part of a regular line. (I was down to one box of 24s!) This is my go-to pencil for reasonably dark lines that don't need re-sharpening every two seconds. Just...pick up a few Tombow erasers while you're at it.

4 people found this helpful

Most Pencils are Terrible. Here Are 3 Pencils You Should Actually Buy — Izza Wei-Haas

# Most Pencils are Terrible. Here Are 3 Pencils You Should Actually Buy

 Jul 16 

Written by Izza Wei-Haas

There are hundreds of pencils, mechanical pencils, and drawing tools on the market. New releases happen constantly, but I've realized something over the years: the best art supplies aren't always the newest—they're the ones you continue reaching for.

I don't believe in building a collection for the sake of collecting. I prefer owning a small set of well-made tools that become part of my creative practice. They're reliable, comfortable to use, and often last for years.

A good pencil isn't just about the graphite. It's about how it feels in your hand, how consistently it performs, and whether it disappears into the background so you can focus on making art.

 

 Collection of premium drawing pencils and sketching tools including Rotring 600, Pentel GraphGear 1000, Blackwing pencils, Tombow MONO Zero eraser, pencil sharpener, graphite lead and sketchbook. 

### What Makes a Pencil Worth Buying?

When I'm choosing a pencil or drawing tool, I look for a few things:

- Comfortable for long drawing sessions
- Durable construction that can handle everyday use and abuse
- Easy to refill or maintain
- A design I vibe with

I've found that spending a little more on a quality tool usually means buying it once instead of replacing cheaper versions over and over.

## The Pencils I Keep Coming Back To

#### Rotring 600 Mechanical Pencil, 0.5mm | $20-$40 usd

This is my most recent mechanical pencil purchase and possibly my favorite desk pencil. If I want precision, this is the pencil I reach for. The all-metal body is incredibly comfortable, and I'm a big fan of the fixed lead guidance sleeve, which helps keep the lead stable while drawing. 

It also comes in some beautiful colorways. I have the all-black version, and it's a dream to draw with.

#### Pentel GraphGear 1000 Mechanical pencil, 0.5mm | $10-$20 usd

I've owned this mechanical pencil for more than ten years, and it's still one of my favorites. The grip section is comfortable and inlaid with soft, latex-free pads. One of the best features is the retractable pencil tip. This has officially become my travel pencil because I can easily throw it into any case without worrying about damaging the tip.

The lead can rotate slightly while drawing, so that's something to be aware of, but it has never been enough of an issue to stop me from using it.

#### Blackwing Wooden Pencils | $34 for a set of 12

I really do get the hype. The graphite is incredibly smooth with a premium feel. I tend to switch between different graphite grades depending on what I'm working on.

- Blackwing Matte (Soft | Modern) — Perfect if you prefer soft, dark lines. I use this one for shading.
- Blackwing Pearl (Balanced | 2B) — Slightly firmer than the Matte and a great everyday option.
- Blackwing 602 (Firm | B) — Great for lighter sketching and finer details. I use this for my initial sketches.
- Blackwing Natural (Extra Firm | HB) — Ideal for long-form writing and detailed line work.

## The Pencil Accessories I Actually Use

A few supporting tools have become permanent members of my art kit.

#### NJK #531S Long Point Pencil Sharpener | $7

This produces one of the cleanest long points I've ever used, and I definitely prefer it over the Blackwing pencil sharpener. They're surprisingly difficult to find in the United States 😔, so if you're visiting Japan, it's absolutely worth seeking one out.

I love that it stores the pencil shavings, it's compact, and the blade stays incredibly sharp. It's my go-to everyday and travel sharpener, and honestly, I'd be lost without it.

#### Blackwing Pencil Guard | $20 for a box of 3

Incredibly useful.Since Blackwing pencils have a proprietary shape, they designed their own pencil guard—and I genuinely think it's a must-have. It protects the pencil point and saves the inside of my bag from getting covered in graphite marks.

#### Kneaded Eraser | $1-$5

A kneaded eraser is one of those tools I can't imagine working without. It's gentle on paper, easy to shape, and perfect for lifting graphite without damaging a drawing. Plus, you don't have to deal with eraser debris.

As a bonus, I also use mine to stabilize fountain pen cartridges while filling them with ink.

#### Tombow Mono Zero Eraser, Round 2.3mm | $5–$7

This is my favorite precision eraser. The small tip makes it easy to erase fine details, clean up sketch lines, or add highlights without disturbing the rest of the drawing. The pen-style body is comfortable to use, and the refills are inexpensive, making it a tool I always have in my drawing bag.

#### Pilot Neox Graphite Lead | $3-$7

For mechanical pencils, this is my favorite lead. It writes smoothly, produces consistent lines, and breaks less often than many alternatives I've tried. I use HB 0.5mm and F 0.5mm.

## Buy Once, Draw for Years

I've learned that creative tools don't have to be disposable. A thoughtfully chosen pencil can become something you use for thousands of sketches, journal entries, and finished drawings.

These are the tools that have earned a permanent place in my studio—not because they're trendy, but because they've proven themselves over years of regular use.

If you're building your own creative toolkit, I'd start with quality over quantity. A handful of dependable pencils will take you much further than a drawer full of supplies you never reach for.

# Blackwing Pencils: A Comprehensive Guide

October 21, 2025 - Posted by Connie to Guides, Pencils, Wooden Pencils

When you try a Blackwing, you’ll know why artists and writers are obsessed with this graphite pencil. Read on to learn why Blackwing Pencils stand out and see limited edition pencils you’ll want to collect.

Form Factor

Blackwing Pencils are known for their flat ferrules.

 Blackwing Pencils have distinctive looks that set them apart from other pencils. Their iconic ferrules (the metal parts at the opposite ends of the graphite) are long and flat. They hold rectangular erasers that can be extended with the metal clips when they wear down, and replaced when they’re used up. 

Blackwing Pencils have unique eraser clips and erasers. They’re also longer than typical pencils.

 The graphite pencils have gold-colored ferrules, while the colored pencils have silver ferrules. The included rubber erasers are black for the Matte, white for the Pearl, pink for the 602, and gray for the Natural. The Colors have gray sand erasers. 

The Matte, Pearl, and 602 models are finished with black, white, or gray lacquer. The Natural has a clear finish so you can see the wood’s texture. The Colors have barrels that match the cores. The Blackwing logo and pencil’s name is gold foiled into the side of each pencil.

Blackwing Pencils are longer than typical pencils, so they don’t fit in standard pen cases. All of the cases in our Extra Long Pencil Cases category can fit Blackwing Pencils.

Lead Grades

Blackwing graphite ranges from soft to extra firm.

 Unlike most brands that use European or American lead grades, Blackwing has four proprietary lead grades, listed below: 

- Soft: The softest and darkest Blackwing graphite. It’s like 3B lead.
- Balanced: Blackwing’s balanced graphite is similar to 2B lead.
- Firm: Firm lead is similar in feel to B lead.
- Extra Firm: The hardest graphite Blackwing offers. It’s the most similar to #2 or HB pencil lead.

Other lead grades are sometimes made for limited edition releases. Check out the Volumes or Special Editions sections to learn more.

Materials

A Blackwing Pencil has a pleasant smell thanks to its incense cedar body.

 All Blackwing Pencils are made from California incense cedar. They have mild, pleasant scents that get stronger when the pencils are sharpened. 

The graphite and wax cores are made in Japan. The graphite uses a formula that’s smoother and softer than most pencil leads. However, they hold their points reasonably well.

Standard Blackwing Pencils

Blackwing Matte Pencils

The Blackwing Matte uses soft and dark graphite.

Blackwing Matte Pencils use the softest and darkest lead. Their buttery cores feel similar to 3B leads and are especially good for art. They can make light marks when used with a gentle touch, but are typically quite dark. Unlike some soft pencils, the Matte Pencils don’t crumble with use. They’re very consistent and sharpen to fine points, but because they’re so soft, they wear down quickly. 

The original Matte Pencils have black bodies with gold-colored ferrules and black erasers. The Green Finish and Red Finish Pencils have copper-colored ferrules and gray erasers.

Graphite: Soft (similar to 3B lead)

Blackwing Pearl Pencils

The Blackwing Pearl stays sharp longer than the Matte Pencil.

 The Blackwing Pearl is a bit harder than the Blackwing Matte, but it’s still soft and dark. It stays sharp longer, so people who enjoy smooth pencils but don’t want to sharpen them as often will prefer the Pearl. Its balance of darkness and hardness makes it a great option for people who want to use the same pencil to write and draw with. 

The original Blackwing Pearl has a pearlescent white finish with a gold ferrule and white eraser. It’s also available with shimmery pink or blue barrels.

Graphite: Balanced (similar to 2B lead)

Blackwing 602 Pencils

The Blackwing 602 is closest to the original Blackwing.

 Ideal for writing, the Blackwing 602 is smoother than a typical writing pencil. It’s the closest in feel to the vintage Eberhard Faber Blackwing. As a tribute, it has the original “Half the Pressure, Twice the Speed” slogan on the barrel. 

The Blackwing 602 has a pearlescent gray finish with a gold ferrule and pink eraser. You can also get them as short pencils that are half the length of the standard 602, so they fit right into pencil cases without needing to wear them down first.

Graphite: Firm (similar to B lead)

Blackwing Natural Pencils

The Blackwing Natural offers the hardest graphite found in the standard Blackwing lineup.

 The newest addition to the standard lineup, the Blackwing Natural Pencil offers the hardest graphite. They’re still smooth, which makes writing with them a pleasant experience. We recommend them to writers who want their pencils to stay sharp as long as possible. 

They’re unpainted with clear matte finishes, letting you appreciate the natural color and pattern of the wood.

Graphite: Extra Firm (similar to HB lead)

Blackwing Colors Colored Pencils

 Blackwing Colors have extra-smooth wax cores.

Blackwing Colors are colored pencil versions of Blackwing Pencils. Their extra smooth wax cores don’t feel “waxy” or become crumbly with use. They’re made from California incense cedar with cores made in Japan. 

The colored pencils include special sand erasers made specifically for the Blackwing’s color cores.

They work best on mildly textured paper, like the kind found in adult coloring books. They also show up well on black paper.

Blackwing Non-Photo Blue & Red Pencils

Blackwing Non-Photo Blue & Red Pencils have useful colored cores.

 These pencils combine the iconic aesthetics of Blackwing Pencils with useful colored cores. The Non-Photo Blue Pencils create light blue lines that won’t appear on scans or photocopies. They can also be removed easily using digital art software. 

The Red Pencils leave vivid marks that are excellent for edits and corrections. Both pencils have colored sand erasers and are available in packs of six.

Blackwing Box Sets

 Blackwing Box Sets are made of luxurious materials and filled with Blackwing Pencils.

 A Blackwing Box Set is a lovely present for a fellow writer or pencil enthusiast—it’s also a great way to treat yourself! The boxes are made from different materials and include twelve pencils. The pencils can be the same types, or you can get mixed varieties. 

The Rustic boxes also include Two-Step Long Point Sharpeners.

When he opened his Pop Shop in 1986, Haring thought of it as a physical extension of his work, a place where everyone was welcome to experience his art. Printed with his iconic colorful dancing figures, Blackwing Volumes Vol. 292 Pencils are tributes to Keith and his enduring legacy.  These Vol. 574 Pencils are tributes to Native American art and the 574 surviving tribes within the United States. Designed in collaboration with Chris Papaan, a Kaw, Osage, and Lakota artist, they feature geometric patterns evocative of the patterns found in the art of many Native American tribes. Blackwing will donate a portion of the proceeds from this release to the Cheyenne River Youth Project and their mission to provide enriching arts programs to Lakota youth. 

Blackwing Volumes Vol. XIX Second Edition Pencils

 These Vol. XIX Pencils are re-releases of pencils from 2020. They celebrate the ratification of the 19th Amendment, which gave women of the United States the right to vote throughout the country, and the ongoing fight to protect voting rights in the United States and around the world.

Vol. 71 Pencils are tributes to the modernist architect Frank Lloyd Wright and his architectural vision. Each pencil has one of four designs based on the perforated window boards commonly found in his iconic Usonian houses. The designs are printed in a muted, mid-century color palette, with the pencils’ natural wood finish showing through the negative space. The number 71 refers to Wright’s age when he constructed his first Usonian home.

## Beschreibung

The Blackwing Natural features an exposed incense cedar barrel with a subtle clear matte finish and our popular extra-firm graphite. Each Blackwing Natural features a gold imprint, grey eraser and the iconic square Blackwing ferrule. Blackwing Natural pencils come in a pack of 12 in a gift box that doubles as a pencil cup.

Sometimes the letters are also preceded by numbers. They make an even more precise statement about the hardness or colour intensity of the pencil. The higher the number, the harder, softer or blacker the pencil is.

### New edition of a cult pencil

Nobody suspected that Eberhard Faber's Blackwing enjoyed a large following among pencil enthusiasts when the American manufacturer discontinued its production in 1998. Only a short time later, the remaining copies were highly traded, so Palomino, another American stationery manufacturer no less steeped in tradition, decided to bring out a modified new edition of the Blackwing. 

### Die Story zu BLACKWING

Blackwing – Die Legende unter den Bleistiften

Der Blackwing Bleistift gilt als Ikone unter den Schreibinstrumenten. Seit seiner Einführung in den 1930er Jahren hat er sich einen legendären Ruf erarbeitet – nicht nur aufgrund seiner aussergewöhnlichen Qualität, sondern auch durch seine prominenten Nutzer. Künstler, Schriftsteller, Musiker und Kreative schwören bis heute auf ihn. Zu seinen berühmtesten Fans zählten Walt Disney, John Steinbeck und Leonard Bernstein. Sie alle schätzten das aussergewöhnlich weiche, präzise Schreibgefühl und das elegante Design des Blackwing.

Was den Blackwing besonders macht, ist die Kombination aus hochwertigem japanischen Graphit, einem langlebigen Holzschaft aus kalifornischer Zeder und der charakteristischen, auswechselbaren Flachradiergummi-Spitze. Diese einzigartige Formgebung ist nicht nur optisch ein Hingucker, sondern bietet auch eine ergonomische Funktionalität.

Nach einer Zeit der Produktionseinstellung wurde der Blackwing 2010 von der Firma Palomino neu aufgelegt – mit dem Ziel, den Kultstatus des Originals zu bewahren und gleichzeitig höchste Qualität neu zu interpretieren. Das Sortiment wurde seitdem erweitert: Neben dem klassischen Blackwing gibt es heute Varianten wie den Blackwing 602 (härter, ideal für lange Schreibarbeiten), den Blackwing Pearl (mittelweich, ideal zum Skizzieren) oder die limitierte Volumes-Serie, die besonderen Persönlichkeiten und kulturellen Ereignissen gewidmet ist.

Der Blackwing ist mehr als nur ein Bleistift – er ist ein Statement für kreative Freiheit, Qualität und zeitloses Design. Wer ihn einmal benutzt hat, erkennt sofort den Unterschied: Das Schreiben wird zum Erlebnis.

„Half the pressure, twice the speed.“ Der berühmte Slogan des Blackwing 602 bringt es auf den Punkt – mit minimalem Druck schreibt und zeichnet man mühelos, flüssig und präzise. Kein Wunder, dass dieser Bleistift zur ersten Wahl für Generationen von kreativen Köpfen geworden ist.
